rounds.candidate_count_scope: Distinct scholarly title/DOI records across the visible first-page results of the six logged query families, before deduplication against the workspace's existing graph.
findings: Exact minimisation of the tilt dual for fixed d_lambda and variable K is already covered in arithmetic complexity by parametric search (Megiddo 1983 at d_lambda=1; Toledo 1993 in fixed dimension with polynomial comparisons); DS19.2's exact-computation scope (fixed K and fixed d_lambda) was narrower than the literature allows. Bit complexity is not covered by either source.

The fixed-tilt interval DP is the classical 1-D k-means DP (Wang-Song 2011) and runs in O(KN) after sorting (Gronlund et al. 2017), improving DS19.2's O(KN^2) statement; weighted points are covered there, exact ties are not.
Design-side D_s duality (Silvey-Titterington 1973; Pukelsheim-Titterington 1983) is a convex-feasible-set template only; the hard-partition interchange fails by exact witnesses at N=3.
limitations: Theorem-targeted triangulation, not a citation-saturation round.
Carstensen 1983 is a secondary record (thesis not read).
No forward-citation traversal was run on Toledo 1993; later fixed-dimension parametric-search and real-RAM-to-bit-complexity results may exist and are logged in gaps.md.

rounds.candidate_count_scope: Distinct textbook and article records returned by the five query families before deduplication.
findings: O6.2-O6.4 are a direct instance of the multivariate delta method for functions of sample means (van der Vaart Thm 3.1; Serfling Sec. 3.3 Thm B; Cramer Ch. 28) combined with the influence-function variance formula (Hampel et al. 1986); no novelty is claimed for the method.

The closed-form influence function of the uncentred correlation ratio with a fixed partition, the RSS identity, and the two-atoms-per-cell characterisation of sigma^2 = 0 were not located as stated in any source; they are recorded as project algebra inside a bridge node, not as a search gap and not as novelty.
The classical eta-squared interval literature (Wishart 1932; Kelley 2007) is normal-theory and centred, and does not transfer.
limitations: Theorem-targeted triangulation, not a citation-saturation round.
No primary text was read; van der Vaart and Serfling theorem numbers rest on secondary quotations, Cramer's on memory, Hampel et al.'s section number is unverified.
Kendall and Stuart Vol. 2 (asymptotic variance of the sample correlation ratio) was not located to a section and is not registered.

papers.title: Principal points
papers.note: Primary text reviewed 31 Aug 2026. Defines globally MSE-optimal principal points; proves the two-point elliptical leading-eigenvector result and dim span <= k-1, but states the k>2 leading principal-subspace result only as a conjecture. No general existence or arbitrary self-consistent-point theorem.

papers.title: Self-consistency: a fundamental concept in statistics
papers.note: Primary text reviewed 31 Aug 2026. Credits Hastie-Stuetzle for the term and defines E[X|Y]=Y. Theorem 4.1 under LCM plus projection-measurability forces the q-dimensional support span of self-consistent Y to be spanned by q covariance eigenvectors, not necessarily the leading q.

papers.title: Principal points and self-consistent points of elliptical distributions
papers.note: Theorem scope cross-checked 31 Aug 2026 against Tarpey-Flury 1996 primary text and later explicit restatements: n principal points of a centered elliptical law spanning dimension q lie in the leading q-eigenspace. Primary proof not retrieved; do not silently extend the leading-eigenspace conclusion to every self-consistent point set.

papers.title: Weak limit theorems for univariate k-mean clustering under a nonregular condition
papers.note: Primary PDF read verbatim 31 Aug 2026: split-function formulation of 1-D k-means over ordered cutpoints, unique global optimum, singular-Hessian nonregular case with n^{1/4} rates. Per-law degeneracy asymptotics, not a class-wide forcing theorem.

papers.title: Efficient and Adaptive Estimation for Semiparametric Models
